title: Priority-staged spill & admission controller for bursty QPS
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: During short-lived spikes (hundreds to thousands QPS for 10-60s) our continuous batching pipeline experiences microbatch saturation and KV cache pressure resulting in either high tail latency or bulk eviction thrashing on GPU memory. Current admission decisions are too coarse: they either accept and cause GPU OOM/evictions or throttle aggressively causing throughput loss.

Goal: Implement a priority-aware, staged admission controller that: (1) assigns lightweight priority slots for critical low-token requests, (2) allows a staged spill path that moves cold KV entries to host DRAM (or quantized compressed storage) for overflow periods, and (3) dynamically lowers microbatch thresholds for noncritical traffic to preserve tail latency for high-priority requests. The controller should integrate with the existing KV cache scoring (recency+model-weight) and the batching runtime so decisions are made per-request with sub-10ms decision latency.

Scope: server-side runtime change + config surface in Console for per-customer priority policies. Runtime changes include: priority slot allocator, staged-spill operator, per-request KV footprint estimator, and an admission policy engine that exposes tunables (slot counts, spill aggressiveness, per-priority batch size ceiling). Console changes out of scope for this ticket but tracked as follow-up.

Constraints & trade-offs: Staged spill reduces eviction churn but increases host->GPU copy latency for spilled cache hits; must weigh cost vs latency for different priorities. Priority slots improve tail for critical requests but may cause starvation; admission controller must strictly enforce soft quotas and fallback to queue-based pacing. Implementation must avoid introducing global locks on hot paths; aim for atomic per-shard counters + lock-free ring for slot allocation.

Success metrics: 95th/99th token latency for P0 traffic stays within SLOs during synthetic burst tests; overall token throughput degradation < 8% for typical workload; GPU memory OOMs eliminated in replayed incident traces.
acceptance_criteria: Priority slots implemented and controllable via runtime flag
Staged spill path that moves selected KV shard entries to host memory exists and can be toggled per node
Admission decisions made with <10ms added decision latency under 99th percentile
Benchmark: under 1k->5k QPS spike replay, P0 99th token latency < target SLO (see attachments), and OOMs = 0
Automated unit and integration tests for slot allocator, spill operator, and estimator
Design doc and runbook added to Confluence with rollback steps
comments: 2026-03-10: Kickoff with runtime and eva teams. Agreed priority definition: P0 = interactive user-facing short requests (<64 tokens), P1 = background/higher-token jobs. Ava to draft design doc.

2026-03-11: Prototype idea: per-shard token-footprint estimator using header metadata instead of full pass — reduces estimator cost to ~200ns/request. Liam to prototype in branch feature/priority-spill. Decision: use atomic counters per shard for slot accounting to avoid global lock.

2026-03-11: Trade-off discussion: Spill-to-host uses lightweight compression (FP16 + 4-bit quant pack) vs memcpy plain — compression reduces host memory but adds CPU cost. Chose compress-by-default for long spikes, plain memcpy for short spikes (configurable threshold).

2026-03-12: Bench results (local): synthetic replay of incident-2026-01-19 with staged spill enabled shows 60% drop in eviction churn and 30% improvement in tails for P0 traffic; CPU for compression increased by ~12%. Uploaded Grafana dashboard link in attachments.

2026-03-13: Code review feedback from Sofia (runtime lead): avoid per-request heap allocations in allocator path; switch to stack-allocated slab and reuse buffers. Also suggested adding telemetry events for 'slot_acquire' and 'spill_evict' for postmortem analysis. Liam updated PR 1123.
2026-03-13: Follow-ups: Console policy UI ticket created (PM-412), and Dedicated autoscaler knobs need to expose 'spill aggressiveness' (ENG-41450).
notes: This ticket is intentionally conservative on rollout: default off, enable via node-level flags, controlled canary on 5% nodes before ramp. A runbook will include steps to disable spill path quickly and revert slot counts.
